$provenance.CLAUDE_PREVIEW_CLASSIFIER_FLOOR: Desktop 1.32352.0, hand-read from W1: `...t.hy(`1129419822`)&&{ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH:`auto`},CLAUDE_PREVIEW_CLASSIFIER_FLOOR:`1`,CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_TOOL_USE_SUMMARIES:...` — a BARE key between the tool-search gate spread and the summaries ternary. No gate, no sessionType branch, no deployment branch, so a first-party Cowork session always receives it. The variable itself is older (the bundled CLI declares it, and the desktop CODE-session runner sets it behind a gate); what is new here is the Cowork spawn setting it unconditionally. ||| Desktop 1.37937.1 / agent 2.1.246: the key is still SET here — the golden value stays "1" because this file records what the spawn CONSTRUCTS — but the agent renamed the flag it reads to CLAUDE_CHROME_CLASSIFIER_FLOOR (and its consumer field previewClassifierFloorEnabled -> chromeClassifierFloorEnabled). Measured: CLAUDE_PREVIEW_CLASSIFIER_FLOOR occurs 3x in native 2.1.241 and 0x in 2.1.246, while CLAUDE_CHROME_CLASSIFIER_FLOOR is 0->present in the 2.1.246 CLAUDE_*:()=> export table. Desktop sets ONLY the old name (the new name appears in the asar solely as the bundled CLI's own export table, never as a spawn key), so on agent 2.1.246 the key the Cowork spawn sets is DEAD and the floor falls through to the GrowthBook default tengu_cowork_chrome_automode_default. The pin stays: it records the spawn contract faithfully, and a Desktop-side rename to the new name must show as a --diff line. Nothing in the harness reads this key behaviourally.
$provenance.CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL / CLAUDE_CO: Desktop 1.37937.0, hand-read from W1: `...CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK:`1`,CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_APPEND_SUBAGENT_PROMPT:`1`,CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL:`1h`,CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL:`5m`,ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H:`1`,...` — two BARE keys with no gate, no sessionType branch and no deployment branch, so a first-party Cowork session always receives them. ADDITIVE: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H is still set alongside them, not replaced. They read 0 times in agent 2.1.241 and 6 times each in 2.1.246, so the contract is live rather than forward-declared.
$provenance.MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_1p_vs_3p: Desktop 1.37937.0 gave this key a SECOND construction site, in the 3p-only branch of W3 (`...i!==void 0&&{MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT:String(i)}`, `i` a chunk-local let). The golden value below is still the W1/1p one: its getter gained a higher-priority term (`zS()??Ec()?.mcpToolTimeoutMs??18e4`, was `rl()?.mcpToolTimeoutMs??18e4`) but zS() reads the `mcp.toolTimeoutSec` USER SETTING and is undefined by default, so the modeled default session still resolves through `??18e4` -> 180000. Re-read by hand 2026-08-26. ||| HOW THE RESOLVER ARRIVES AT 180000, stated because it is right for a reason narrower than it looks: resolveStringArg's `??`-fallback regex is greedy, so it captures the LAST fallback in the chain (18e4) and IGNORES the higher-priority zS() term entirely. It does not model the precedence. That coincides with the value a real session receives ONLY while every higher-priority term is undefined by default — verified here: zS() reads `W().mcp.toolTimeoutSec`, a USER SETTING that is undefined unless set, and Ec() is the same shape. If a future build gives one of them a non-undefined default, this file would still read 180000 and nothing would flag. Re-check the chain, not just the final fallback, whenever this getter changes.
$provenance.CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT: Desktop 1.40609.0 / agent 2.1.247, re-read by hand: W2's deployment ternary was HOISTED into a same-chunk helper — `function uH(e){return e===`3p`?`claude-desktop-3p`:`claude-desktop`}`, called as `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:uH(n.type)` (was the inline `n.type===`3p`?...` through 1.37937.1). Same predicate, same two literals: a pure refactor. The golden value below is unchanged and is NOT W2's value in any case — W1 is applied last and hard-sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:`local-agent`` after the `t.Cl({...})` spread, so the 1p session receives `local-agent` on both builds. resolveSpawnValue resolves the hoisted form by inlining the callee body from the window's OWN chunk (B13) and refuses any other body; a bare 2-char minified name hopped against the joined bundle would land elsewhere.
